_readme: The demo tour (UI_SPEC.md section 12). Edit the words freely. target: a data-tour name on the page at route (null: a dialog in the middle). {streak} is replaced with the streak on screen. lineage: only names that exist in the code: kind is source, endpoint, dag, task, table or function; api/tests/test_tour_lineage.py checks every one.

steps.title: One app, three sources
steps.text: My training, running and nutrition data lives in separate apps that don't talk to each other, so I built a pipeline that joins them.
steps.built: React and FastAPI over a PostgreSQL warehouse, loaded by Airflow. Everything here is synthetic data, built by the real pipeline.

steps.title: A {streak}-day streak
steps.text: A day counts when food is logged within budget and there's a workout. Rest days and recovery days are allowed, within rules.
steps.built: One SQL function decides every day's status; the streak is a window-function count over it.

steps.title: Food, from Apple Health
steps.text: An iPhone Shortcut pushes each meal's calories and protein after it's logged.
steps.built: A token-protected POST, checked sample by sample. A batch sent twice is recognised by its SHA-256 and stored once.

steps.title: Every workout, from Strava
steps.text: Runs and walks from the Apple Watch, and lifting sessions logged in Hevy, all arrive through Strava.
steps.built: Airflow syncs Strava every hour: the list call, then each activity's detail, picking up from a watermark. Loads are idempotent upserts.

steps.title: Free text in, set-level records out
steps.text: Hevy writes each workout into the Strava description as plain text. A parser turns it into one row per set.
steps.built: A small grammar with golden tests. A line it can't read goes to quarantine with a reason; the rest of the session still loads.

steps.title: The pipeline watches itself
steps.text: When each source last synced, failed runs, quarantined lines, and 15 data-quality checks. This demo has a timed-out sync and its retry, and a few warnings.
steps.built: Every run is a row in ops.pipeline_runs. A second DAG runs the checks, each one a plain SQL file, and stores the results.

steps.title: That's the tour
steps.text: Look around: every page works, and nothing you change is saved.
steps.built: The demo is its own service on its own database, with a read-only role and no real credentials.
